clue.text: More than one sweet smell annoys

blocks.note: to hum is informal British for to smell bad
bugs means irritates

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a sweet-scented whiff is getting on their nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet smell' reads as a phrase, but the definition stops at 'sweet'; 'smell' starts the wordplay as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbugs are traditional British boiled mint sweets, and the plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Manual labourer is no longer spinning tool

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so the word for no longer existing is turned back to front

blocks.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
what is no longer the case was

explanation.surface: A worker with a spinning tool is out of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning tool' looks like a phrase for a drill, but spinning is the reversal signal and the definition is just 'tool'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsaw is a saw worked by one hand, a woodworking tool.

clue.text: Hopelessly romantic, with no time for the original Telegraph man?

indicators.note: with no says a letter is taken away from the word
hopelessly suggests a jumbled, muddled state, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A dreamy question about the first journalist working at the Telegraph, too busy for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is this paper, but here it is wireless telegraphy, which Guglielmo Marconi pioneered.
explanation.definitionFit: Marconi developed wireless telegraphy in the 1890s, so he was the original man behind radio telegraph messages.

clue.text: Trouble afoot when bishop leaves wedding

indicators.note: when someone leaves they go away, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Something is going wrong once the clergyman walks out of the marriage ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble afoot' sounds like brewing mischief, but it is literally a foot problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a marriage, the joining of two people, so it can stand for a wedding.

clue.text: Does one collect the views of suckers?

definitions.text: Does one collect the views of suckers?

blocks.clueFragment: Does one collect the views of suckers?
blocks.note: surface: a survey of gullible people, suckers meaning dupes
setter's reading: suckers are drinking tubes people suck through, so a survey named after them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' reads as dupes, but it hints at drinking tubes, giving the name of an informal opinion survey.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an unofficial show of opinion, a quick sampling of people's views.

clue.text: "Stop!" I called, taking only part that's contemporary

indicators.note: taking only part of the quoted words means the letters run inside them, across the word gap

blocks.note: the letters sit inside these words, dropping the first S and the final LED

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for a halt, then only part of what they called is current.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical deals with current affairs, so it is contemporary in the sense of up to date.

clue.text: Model entertaining males in private

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so the plaything holds the men inside

blocks.note: a toy can be a model, such as a toy train
M is male, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A fashion model hosting men behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In private' looks like a phrase meaning secretly; 'private' is the definition, the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, is the traditional nickname for a private soldier in the British Army.

clue.text: Cut up rubbish material used for suits

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to snip is to cut
tripe means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A tailor slices up worthless cloth meant for business suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripe is cloth woven with thin stripes, the classic fabric for City business suits.

clue.text: Fancy cooking ham and rice

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is in the mood to make a dish of ham with rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning want; it is a noun, a flight of imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an illusory fantasy or wild dream, which is one sense of the noun fancy.

clue.text: Row over time for descent

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first word sits on top of the second

blocks.note: a row is a line, as in a line of chairs
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A quarrel that drags on for ages before going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument, but it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is a family line of ancestry, which is what descent means in the sense of being descended from someone.

clue.text: More studious king in Flanders? That is right

indicators.note: in places the royal letter inside the neighbour's name

blocks.note: Ned Flanders is Homer's neighbour in The Simpsons
R for Rex, Latin for king
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A question about a scholarly monarch in the Low Countries.
explanation.walkthrough: Flanders looks like the Belgian region, but it is Ned Flanders, the devout neighbour in The Simpsons.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is an obsessive swot, so nerdier is a comparative meaning more bookish or studious.

clue.text: Husband and child maybe touring island residence

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the child word wraps around the island letter

blocks.note: as in 'man and wife', man can mean husband
a son is one example of a child
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A married couple and their son go sightseeing round an island's grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansion is a large, impressive house, a grand kind of residence.

clue.text: Scottish town with small hill? You must be joking

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
'No way!' is the incredulous reply

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs on hearing that a Scottish town has only a little hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Stornoway is the main town of the Isle of Lewis in Scotland's Outer Hebrides.

clue.text: Article cheers Greek character

blocks.note: the definite article
ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece applauds a person from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but here it means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: What one of Bob Marley's group does? Complains!

definitions.text: What one of Bob Marley's group does?

blocks.clueFragment: What one of Bob Marley's group does?
blocks.note: Marley's band was the Wailers, so playfully a member is one who does this
to moan or protest loudly

explanation.surface: A question about what a reggae band member does, then an exclamation of complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Marley and the Wailers were the Jamaican reggae group; the first definition is a playful back-formation from their name.
explanation.definitionFit: To wail is to cry out in grief or protest, so the verb also covers someone grumbling loudly.

clue.text: In Germany, they finally sang hot opera

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the next word

blocks.note: sie is German for they
the last letter of sang
fried can mean hot, as when someone is fried in the sun

explanation.surface: A German company finished their warm performance of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried is the third opera of Wagner's Ring cycle, named after its hero.

clue.text: Stubborn botanist set out facing east

indicators.note: to set something out is to lay it out afresh in a new arrangement
facing puts the compass letter up against the end of the rearranged word

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A determined plant scientist plants themselves looking eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate and stubborn are synonyms for refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Band on strike in seedy venue

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first word is placed above the second

blocks.note: a strip is a narrow band, of cloth for example
to club is to hit or strike

explanation.surface: A rock group stage a walkout in a sleazy nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band on strike' reads as musicians refusing to play; band is a strip and strike is a verb, to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip club is a nightclub with striptease shows, the kind of seedy place the definition describes.

clue.text: Screw fitting around well worker initially removed

indicators.note: removed tells us a letter named just before it is taken away
around means the word for fitting is wrapped about the shortened word
'initially' keeps only the first letter of 'worker'

blocks.note: proper means suitable or fitting
taken as written
the first letter of worker

explanation.surface: A screw is being fitted around a well after the labourer first takes it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like part of a screw-fixing scene, but it is an adjective meaning appropriate, and the well loses its opening letter before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's propeller is called a screw, since it drives through water by rotating like a screw thread.

clue.text: What the heart's doing when doing this to iron?

definitions.text: What the heart's doing when doing this to iron?

blocks.note: surface: what a beating heart does with blood
setter's reading: the same verb with iron makes the gym phrase for lifting weights, which gets the heart racing

explanation.walkthrough: The verb serves twice: it is what the heart does to blood, and paired with iron it is slang for weight training.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is a muscular pump, and 'pumping iron' is the idiom for lifting weights at the gym.

clue.text: Busy hotel with strange gent going round in circles

indicators.note: strange suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are set in an odd order
going round means the rings are placed either side, enclosing the jumbled letters

blocks.note: each circle is an O, two of them for the plural
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frantic hotel where an odd man paces round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go is an idiom for being constantly active and busy.

clue.text: Follow largely unseen criminal

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the last letter is cut
something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tailing a criminal who mostly stays out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, so it means to follow in time or sequence.

clue.text: Part of group infiltrated by FBI agents

indicators.note: a group infiltrated by agents has them inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a set is a group
G-men is American slang for FBI agents

explanation.surface: Some members of an organisation have been penetrated by federal agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of group' reads as a hidden-word signal, but 'Part' is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a section or portion of a whole, that is, a part.

clue.text: Hospital department duplicated drug agreement

blocks.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
the department repeated
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A hospital ward accidentally doubles a patient's medication deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale, so an agreement.

clue.text: Test provided theme

blocks.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
provided can mean 'on condition that', that is if

explanation.surface: An exam set a subject for the candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea or pattern in art, music or writing, which is a theme.

clue.text: Spooner's collapse stretched such as the Premier League?

indicators.note: Spooner was the Oxford don famed for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

blocks.note: a flop is a collapse and taut is tight; say the pair with their opening sounds exchanged

explanation.surface: A football fan worries that the top league is overstretched and about to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of FLOP TIGHT: FL and T trade places to give TOP FLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: England's Premier League is the highest division of football, the top flight; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Smothered to some extent in that place

indicators.note: to some extent means only a portion of the word is used, the run of letters within it

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word, after SMO and before D

explanation.surface: Someone was partly suffocated at a particular spot.
explanation.definitionFit: There is the adverb meaning at or in that place, as opposed to here.

clue.text: Caught in temptation to make money

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the word for temptation

blocks.note: a lure is an enticement or temptation
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone trapped by the urge to get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially gained dishonestly, as in 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Invite misery, revealing list

indicators.note: revealing means the clue words open up to show a word sitting within them

blocks.note: the letters run inside these words, after INV and before RY

explanation.surface: Asking for unhappiness exposes a catalogue of woes.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, so it is a verb meaning to list.

clue.text: Stand in front of a congregation?

definitions.text: Stand in front of a congregation?

blocks.clueFragment: Stand in front of a congregation?
blocks.note: surface: an instruction to get up and face the people in church, as a preacher does
setter's reading: stand is a noun, a piece of church furniture positioned facing the pews

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' reads as a verb telling someone to rise; it is a noun naming an object that holds a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a reading desk from which the Bible is read aloud to worshippers in church.

clue.text: Northerner say running back at all costs?

indicators.note: running back means going in the reverse direction, so the abbreviation is read right to left

blocks.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means
as in 'do or die', meaning whatever it takes

explanation.surface: A northerner, perhaps, sprinting back whatever the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it hints at the definition being an example, but it gives EG, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Geordie is a native of Tyneside, around Newcastle in north-east England, so a northerner.

clue.text: Inspire remake of The Bear

indicators.note: a remake of a film reshoots it in a new version, so the letters are rebuilt in fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new version of the TV show The Bear might motivate viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspire in its literal sense means to breathe in, inhaling air.
